clinical_significance: Flexor tenosynovitis raises pressure within the carpal tunnel (itself provoked further by wrist flexion and extension) and can precipitate or worsen carpal tunnel syndrome. The ulnar bursa communicates with the radial bursa (flexor pollicis longus) at the wrist in a proportion of hands, which is the anatomical basis of the horseshoe abscess (infection tracking from the thumb to the little finger, or vice versa, via the two communicating bursae).
function: Synovial sheath surrounding the four flexor digitorum superficialis and four flexor digitorum profundus tendons as they cross the wrist inside the carpal tunnel, reducing friction between the tendons and against the flexor retinaculum during finger and wrist flexion. Runs from about 2-3 cm proximal to the flexor retinaculum to the mid-palm, continuous distally with the little finger's digital flexor sheath.
source: Simons, Travell & Simons (1999) Trigger Point Manual, 2nd ed., Vol. 1; Donnelly et al. (2019) 3rd ed. -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference (wrist_muscles_reference_v2.html), Table 3 ('Tunnels, sheaths and bursae at the wrist') and the flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor pollicis longus profiles, citing Standring 2021, Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed., ch. 50-51, and Green's Operative Hand Surgery 8th ed. (2022) for the horseshoe-abscess mechanism; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998) for the Latin name.

name_ta: Vagina tendinis musculi flexoris pollicis longi
clinical_significance: Radial bursa tenosynovitis (flexor pollicis longus tenosynovitis) presents as pain and swelling along the radial volar wrist and thumb. It communicates with the ulnar bursa at the wrist in a proportion of hands, the anatomical basis of the horseshoe abscess by which a thumb (or little finger) flexor sheath infection tracks to the little finger (or thumb) via the two communicating bursae.
function: Synovial sheath surrounding the flexor pollicis longus tendon as it is the most radial structure in the carpal tunnel, continuing distally into the thumb through the A1, oblique and A2 pulleys to the distal phalanx, reducing friction between the tendon and the carpal tunnel/thumb pulley system.
source: Simons, Travell & Simons (1999) Trigger Point Manual, 2nd ed., Vol. 1; Donnelly et al. (2019) 3rd ed. -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference (wrist_muscles_reference_v2.html), Table 3 ('Tunnels, sheaths and bursae at the wrist') and the flexor pollicis longus profile, citing Standring 2021, Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed., ch. 50-51, and Green's Operative Hand Surgery 8th ed. (2022) for the horseshoe-abscess mechanism; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998) for the Latin name.
